newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--Government's economic team will have decided its basic alternatives for the 1997 budget in 15-20 days.

--Economy wakes up from its slumber. Building activity in first seven months of 1996 shows impressive increase of 25.4 percent nationwide (43.4 percent in Attica), attributed in part to significant decrease in interest rates on housing loans.

--Lukewarm denial of new taxes. While the rumours of forthcoming taxation of state titles continue, the government is seriously considering how to deal with the public debt, either with the issue of zero coupons or fixed-rate seven-year bonds.

--Development ministry sources say the problems threatening Siemens' Thessaloniki plant with closure will be dealt with soon, with long-term contracts with Greek telecommunications organisation (OTE).
--Shipowners ask merchant marine for drastic reduction in operating costs of vessels of all categories.
IMERISIA
--Government sets target of 10.3 percent interest rates for 1997, saying that the public debt's interest rate levels is the key to the successful implementation of the budget.
--Budget foresees wage increases of 4.0 percent in two instalments with corrective increase of 3.0 percent for public sector.
--Immediate funding and decreased social security contributions will be the government's incentives to firms to create jobs for young people.
KERDOS
--Government denies taxation of state titles but taxing large real estate holdings still an open question.
--Amendment to developmental law will give new investment incentives for tourism.
--Foreign exchange loans continue to be popular with both business and consumers.
--TVX Gold considering abandoning Kassandra mines project if local objections continue, threatening the largest single private investment project by foreign operator in recent years.
EXPRESS
--Wave of mergers currently in progress in Greece
--Commission rejection for further funding for Inter-European networks projects will further burden the economy and budget.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis orders economic team to look at drastically reducing the farm ministry's budget.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Financing of major road networks threatened as European Commission cuts further funding from Inter-European Networks.
--As TVX Gold threatens to abandon the Kassandra project, US paper Wall Street Journal reveals 'why foreign firms are fleeing Greece'. Major reasons, it says, are red tape and labour costs.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
